criteria.expectation: The report identifies that TideSync.refresh() calls WidgetCenter.shared.reloadAllTimelines() before SharedStore.save(snapshot), so the widget's getTimeline can read the previous snapshot (an ordering bug), and names this as the primary cause of the one-refresh-behind symptom.

The report cites App/TideSync.swift with the line numbers or quoted lines of the reload call and the later save call, and ties them to the widget's SharedStore.load() in Widget/TideWidget.swift getTimeline.
The report recommends persisting the snapshot (SharedStore.save) before calling reloadAllTimelines (or reloadTimelines(ofKind:)).
The report checks the App Group id and suite name across both entitlements files and SharedStore.swift and states they match (not a cause), rather than claiming a mismatch.

The report does not state as certain that the widget will display stale data on device or that this is the only cause; it frames the ordering as a race/likely cause supported by the source, with hedging proportional to the evidence.

The report explicitly states that it is a source-only review and that runtime behavior (WidgetKit reload scheduling, device timing, widget refresh budget, TestFlight signing/entitlement provisioning) was not built, run, or observed.
The report does not claim to have edited, created, or deleted any input files, and proposes changes only as recommendations or diffs in the report.

The report does not assert as a confirmed defect any reload-before-write ordering, App Group id/suite mismatch, or other cause of stale widget data; it may note that save precedes reloadAllTimelines correctly and that group ids match.

The report lists what could not be verified from source alone, such as runtime reload timing, provisioning profiles actually containing the App Group, WidgetKit budget throttling, and the API/networking behavior.

Any extra suggestions (e.g. reloadTimelines(ofKind:), force-unwrapped UserDefaults, error handling, timeline policy) are explicitly labeled optional or low priority and the report does not demand a rewrite or call the code broken.
The report does not claim to have edited, created, or deleted any input files.
